newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish Handlowy sees up to four stable investors.
newsitem.headline: Polish Handlowy sees up to four stable investors.

text.p: Poland's Bank Handlowy expects 27,859,000 shares being offered by the state treasury in a so-called stable tranche, to go to three or four foreign investors, possibly financial institutions, its president said.
Poland is offering a total of 95 percent or 61,750,000 shares of Handlowy in a privatisation scheme which begins in late May. Stable investors would be obliged not to sell the shares for three years.

"In the tranche for stable investors I expect that the shares would be alloted to three or four foreign investors, possibly from the finance sector," the bank's president, Cezary Stypulkowski, told Reuters on Thursday.
Poland is offering 19,500,000 of Handlowy in the institutional investor tranche, 9,750,000 shares in individual investors tranche and 4,641,000 for employees.
The bank earlier said the price for the stable investor tranche would be set in negotiations with the investors and the shares could be allotted by the end of the year.
Stypulkowski also said the bank was hoping some of its clients would buy shares in the individual investor tranche.
"We hope some of our clients... will buy the shares in the public offer. Such a correlation of mutual ties is extremely important and it stabilises relations between a bank and a client," he said.
